import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Due to the small and somewhat repetitive nature of the sample data,
# a grouped bar plot comparing key metrics across a categorical variable
# like 'Occupation' can effectively illustrate potential differences.

# Calculate the mean for 'Sleep Duration' and 'Quality of Sleep' by 'Occupation'
df_agg = df.groupby('Occupation')[['Sleep Duration', 'Quality of Sleep']].mean().reset_index()

# Melt the DataFrame to long format for easier plotting with seaborn.barplot
df_melted = df_agg.melt(id_vars='Occupation', var_name='Metric', value_name='Average Value')

# Set a style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the grouped bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.barplot(
    data=df_melted,
    x='Occupation',
    y='Average Value',
    hue='Metric',
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Average Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep by Occupation', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Average Value', fontsize=12)

plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(title='Sleep Metric', title_fontsize='12', fontsize='10', loc='upper right')
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
